sections.heading: 1. Once or twice a week
lines: ① Start with 1–2 sessions a week.
② Slot them on easy or rest days.
③ No hard session the day before a long run.
④ Focus: hips, calves, single-leg work, breathing.

sections.heading: 2. Get it checked first if…
lines: Pain changes how you run, or the same spot

slides.title:
Same spot hurting

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Late in every 10k, Toto's landings start to wobble. He did bump up his kilometres this month.

Every run is thousands of similar steps, and running is basically hopping from one leg to the other. Most running niggles come from doing more than your body is ready for, so building strength and control alongside your running makes a lot of sense.

Pilates trains hips, glutes and calves for single-leg control, plus a trunk that stays steady while your limbs move. Start with one or two sessions a week on easy days, and skip hard sessions before a long run.

Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physio starts with an assessment of how you move. Book online via the link in bio 🏃
